He played college basketball for [[Santa Monica College]] and [[Cal Poly Mustangs men's basketball|Cal Poly]]. ==High school career== Nwaba attended [[University High School (Los Angeles)|University High School]] in [[Los Angeles]], where he was a two-time All-Western League Most Valuable Player honoree and all-league first team selection. As a senior in 2010–11, he averaged 22.0 points and 11.5 rebounds per game.{{cite web|url=http://www.gopoly.com/sports/mbkb/2015-16/bios/nwaba_david_wl20|title=David Nwaba – Cal Poly|work=gopoly.com|access-date=February 28, 2017|archive-date=March 7, 2017|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170307055113/http://www.gopoly.com/sports/mbkb/2015-16/bios/nwaba_david_wl20|url-status=dead}} ==College career== While initially joining [[Hawaii Pacific Sharks|Hawaii Pacific]], Nwaba [[Redshirt (college sports)|redshirted]] the 2011–12 season and transferred to [[Santa Monica College]] in 2012. In 2012–13, he was named [[Western State Conference]] South Division Player of the Year and to the All-[[California Community College Athletic Association]] state first team after averaging 20.5 points, 8.8 rebounds and 2.5 assists per game. In 2013, Nwaba transferred again, this time to [[Cal Poly Mustangs men's basketball|Cal Poly]]. As a sophomore in 2013–14, he appeared in all 34 games with 30 starts and finished eighth among [[Big West Conference]] players and 59th among [[NCAA Division I]] players with a team-leading 52.6 (140-for-266) field-goal percentage.{{Cite news |last=Scroggin |first=Joshua D. |date=January 21, 2015 |title=Nwaba has green light on 3s now |pages=S1 |work=The Tribune (San Luis Obispo, CA)}} He also finished second in the lineup with 11.7 points and 4.8 rebounds per game and 21 blocks. He was named to Big West All-Tournament Team after averaging 14.0 points and shooting 72.7 (16-for-22) percent from the floor in three contests. On December 14, 2013, he scored a career-high 22 points on 11-for-13 shooting against [[Cal State Dominguez Hills Toros|Cal State Dominguez Hills]]. As a junior in 2014–15, Nwaba finished second in Cal Poly's lineup and 15th among Big West Conference players with 11.4 points per game. He also averaged 4.7 rebounds and had 31 steals at 1.3 per game. He recorded 16 double-digit scoring games, including a season-high 21 points against [[Gonzaga Bulldogs men's basketball|Gonzaga]] on December 20, 2014. As a senior in 2015–16, Nwaba earned All-Big West Honorable Mention selection after averaging 12.5 points, 6.3 rebounds, 3.5 assists and 1.2 steals in 30 games.{{cite web|url=https://www.sports-reference.com/cbb/players/david-nwaba-1.html|title=David Nwaba College Stats|work=Sports-Reference.com|access-date=February 28, 2017}} At the end of his Cal Poly career, Nwaba ranked 15th in program history in rebounds with a total of 465 and was one of 23 players to score more than 1,000 career points.{{cite web|last=Ahmed|first=Naba|url=http://mustangnews.net/former-cal-poly-guard-david-nwaba-joins-los-angeles-d-fenders/|title=Former Cal Poly guard David Nwaba joins Los Angeles D-Fenders|work=mustangnews.net|date=December 15, 2016|access-date=February 28, 2017}} ==Professional career== ===Los Angeles D-Fenders (2016–2017)=== After graduating from Cal Poly in spring 2016 with a sociology degree, Nwaba headed to [[Reno, Nevada]], to try out for the [[NBA G League|NBA Development League]]'s [[Reno Bighorns]]. The Bighorns were awarded his rights but later traded those rights to the [[South Bay Lakers|Los Angeles D-Fenders]] on October 30, 2016.{{cite web|first=Ryan|last=Primeaux|url=http://losangeles.dleague.nba.com/news/161030-d-fenders-finalize-training-camp-roster/|title=D-Fenders Finalize Training Camp Roster and Schedule|work=NBA.com|date=October 30, 2016|access-date=February 28, 2017|archive-date=March 5, 2017|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170305002523/http://losangeles.dleague.nba.com/news/161030-d-fenders-finalize-training-camp-roster/|url-status=dead}} Nwaba joined the D-Fenders for training camp and made the opening-night roster.{{cite web|first=Ryan|last=Primeaux|url=http://losangeles.dleague.nba.com/news/161110-dfenders-final-roster/|title=D-Fenders Set Opening Night Roster|work=NBA.com|date=November 10, 2016|access-date=February 28, 2017|archive-date=December 21, 2016|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20161221033752/http://losangeles.dleague.nba.com/news/161110-dfenders-final-roster/|url-status=dead}} In his G-League debut on November 11, 2016, Nwaba played 21 minutes and recorded 11 points, 7 rebounds, 3 blocks and 1 steal as the D-Fenders defeated the [[Iowa Energy]] 127 - 98.{{cite web | title=IWA vs LAD | url=https://stats.gleague.nba.com/game/2021600004/ }} Playing a total of 40 regular season games for the D-Fenders in the 2016 - 2017 season, Nwaba averaged 14.1 points and 6.9 rebounds in 28.7 minutes per game. The team would make the playoffs and despite Nwaba's averages of 23.3 points, 8.3 rebounds and 2.3 assists, they would be eliminated in the first round by the [[Rio Grande Valley Vipers]] in three games. Nwaba was assigned to the D-Fenders four times during his rookie season with the Lakers.{{cite web|url=http://dleague.nba.com/assignments/|title=2016-17 NBA Assignments|work=NBA.com|access-date=April 14, 2017|archive-date=January 26, 2017|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170126075350/http://dleague.nba.com/assignments/|url-status=dead}} ===Los Angeles Lakers (2017)=== On February 28, 2017, Nwaba signed a 10-day contract with the [[Los Angeles Lakers]].{{cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/lakers/releases/170228-lakers-sign-david-nwaba|title=Lakers Sign David Nwaba|work=NBA.com|date=February 28, 2017|access-date=February 28, 2017}} That night, Nwaba made his NBA debut in a 109–104 loss to the [[Charlotte Hornets]], playing a little over five minutes and only recording one rebound as a statistic.{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/recap?gameId=400900300|title=Kemba Walker scores 30, Hornets rally past Lakers, 109-104|work=ESPN.com|date=February 28, 2017|access-date=March 1, 2017}} On March 11, 2017, he signed a second 10-day contract with the Lakers.{{cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/lakers/releases/170311nwaba-second-10-day|title=Lakers Sign David Nwaba to Second 10-Day Contract|work=NBA.com|date=March 11, 2017|access-date=March 11, 2017}} He made his first start for the Lakers a day later, recording 6 points, 1 rebound and 1 block in a 118–116 loss to the [[Philadelphia 76ers]].{{cite web|url=https://www.basketball-reference.com/players/n/nwabada01/gamelog/2017|title=David Nwaba 2016-17 Game Log|work=Basketball-Reference.com|access-date=March 14, 2017}} On March 21, 2017, he signed a multi-year contract with the Lakers.{{cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/lakers/releases/170321-lakers-sign-nwaba|title=Lakers Sign David Nwaba to Multi-Year Contract|work=NBA.com|date=March 21, 2017|access-date=March 21, 2017}} During his rookie season with the Lakers, Nwaba played 20 games with the team (having a 5 - 15 record for those 20 games) averaging 6.0 points and 3.2 rebounds in 19.9 minutes. On July 12, 2017, he was waived by the Lakers.{{cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/lakers/releases/170712nwaba-waive|title=Lakers Waive David Nwaba|work=NBA.com|date=July 12, 2017|access-date=July 12, 2017}} ===Chicago Bulls (2017–2018)=== On July 14, 2017, Nwaba was claimed off waivers by the [[Chicago Bulls]].{{cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/bulls/bulls-claim-nwaba|title=BULLS CLAIM DAVID NWABA|work=NBA.com|date=July 14, 2017|access-date=July 14, 2017}} Early in the 2017 season, Nwaba entered the starting lineup multiple times and was lauded by his teammates for his ability to contest shots.{{cite web|url=http://www.chicagotribune.com/sports/basketball/bulls/ct-david-nwaba-bulls-notes-spt-1028-20171027-story.html|title=Unheralded David Nwaba has made an impact for Bulls early in season|work=Chicago Tribune|date=October 27, 2017|access-date=November 3, 2017}} On February 22, 2018, Nwaba scored a career-high 21 points while also grabbing 9 rebounds in a 115 - 116 loss against the [[Philadelphia 76ers]].{{Cite news|url=https://www.cbssports.com/fantasy/basketball/news/bulls-david-nwaba-scores-career-high-21-points-thursday/|title=Bulls' David Nwaba: Scores career-high 21 points Thursday|date=February 23, 2018|work=CBS Sports|access-date=February 23, 2018|language=en}} Nwaba's time with the Bulls would be his most productive as he played (and started) the most games of his career in a season with the Bulls and averaged a career high in minutes, rebounds and assists per game. ===Cleveland Cavaliers (2018–2019)=== [[File:David Nwaba 2018.jpg|thumb|200px|right|Nwaba (left) in the 2018 Cleveland Cavaliers Wine & Gold Scrimmage]] On September 8, 2018, Nwaba signed with the [[Cleveland Cavaliers]].{{cite web|title=Cavaliers Sign David Nwaba|url=https://www.nba.com/cavaliers/releases/nwaba-signing-180908|website=NBA.com|access-date=September 8, 2018|date=September 8, 2018}} From November 26, 2018 to December 10, 2018, Nwaba missed nine games due to right knee soreness. He returned and played seven games for the team, averaging 5.5 points and 2.8 rebounds in those 7 games. Unfortunately, he would face more nagging injuries and would miss another 18 games from December 26, 2018 to January 29, 2019 due to a sprained left ankle.{{cite web | title=Despite two injuries, Cavaliers' David Nwaba believes he still has time to prove himself | url=https://www.beaconjournal.com/story/sports/pro/cavs/2019/02/01/despite-two-injuries-cavaliers-david/6137508007/ }} He returned to finish the remaining 30 games for the Cavs' regular season (starting in 8 of those games) as the Cavs finished with a 19 - 63 record. ===Brooklyn Nets (2019–2020)=== On July 17, 2019, Nwaba signed with the [[Brooklyn Nets]].{{cite web |title=Brooklyn Nets Sign David Nwaba |url=https://www.nba.com/nets/news/2019/07/17/brooklyn-nets-sign-david-nwaba |website=NBA.com |access-date=July 17, 2019 |date=July 17, 2019}} Nwaba played in 20 of the Nets' first 28 games of the season and averaged 5.2 points and 2.3 rebounds in those 20 games. On December 19, Nwaba suffered a season-ending [[Achilles tendon rupture|Achilles tear]] in a game against the [[San Antonio Spurs]].{{cite web |last1=Winfield |first1=Kristian |last2=Covert |first2=Adrian |title=David Nwaba suffers torn Achilles in 4th quarter against Spurs |url=https://www.nydailynews.com/sports/basketball/nets/ny-david-nwaba-torn-achilles-injury-nets-spurs-kevin-durant-20191220-dl4vnc2dcvgf5ecw5sv4a4c7xa-story.html |website=New York Daily News |access-date=December 20, 2019 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20191220114013/https://www.nydailynews.com/sports/basketball/nets/ny-david-nwaba-torn-achilles-injury-nets-spurs-kevin-durant-20191220-dl4vnc2dcvgf5ecw5sv4a4c7xa-story.html |archive-date=December 20, 2019 |date=December 19, 2019}} Two weeks after the ankle Achilles tear, on January 3, 2020, Nwaba was waived by the Nets.{{cite web |title=Brooklyn Nets Waive David Nwaba |url=https://www.nba.com/nets/news/2020/01/03/brooklyn-nets-waive-david-nwaba |website=NBA.com |access-date=January 3, 2020 |date=January 3, 2020}} ===Houston Rockets (2020–2022)=== On June 23, 2020, Nwaba signed a two-year deal with the [[Houston Rockets]].{{cite web |title=Rockets Sign Free Agent David Nwaba |url=https://www.nba.com/rockets/news/rockets-sign-free-agent-david-nwaba-0 |website=NBA.com |access-date=June 23, 2020 |date=June 23, 2020}} On February 22, 2021, the Rockets suffered their 11th loss in a row by losing 84 - 133 to the [[Memphis Grizzlies]]. In that game, Nwaba injured his wrist on a dunk attempt and was expected to miss 6 weeks of playing action.{{cite web | title=David Nwaba plays through pain in loss for the short-handed Rockets | date=March 13, 2021 | url=https://www.thedreamshake.com/2021/3/13/22329074/david-nwaba-plays-through-pain-in-loss-for-the-short-handed-rockets }} He would miss the next three games initially then returned to the team to play against the [[Utah Jazz]] on March 12 (losing to the Jazz by 15) and the [[Boston Celtics]] on March 14 (losing to the Celtics by 27). After those losses, Nwaba would be sidelined for the rest of the season as the Rockets finished with a league-worst 17 - 55 record. On September 30, 2022, Nwaba was traded, along with [[Trey Burke]], [[Sterling Brown (basketball)|Sterling Brown]], and [[Marquese Chriss]], to the [[Oklahoma City Thunder]] in exchange for [[Derrick Favors]], [[Ty Jerome]], [[Maurice Harkless]], [[Théo Maledon]] and a future second-round pick.{{cite web |title=Thunder Acquires Sterling Brown, Trey Burke, Marquese Chriss, David Nwaba and Generates Two Trade Exceptions |url=https://www.nba.com/thunder/news/release-acquisitions-220930 |website=NBA.com |date= September 30, 2022 |access-date=October 1, 2022}} Nwaba would be waived by the Thunder on October 17, 2022, two days before the team's season-opener.{{Cite web |title=OKC Thunder news: David Nwaba, Trey Burke, Marquese Chriss waived |url=https://okcthunderwire.usatoday.com/2022/10/17/okc-thunder-news-david-nwaba-trey-burke-marquese-chriss-waived/ |access-date=December 18, 2022 |website=USA Today|date=October 17, 2022 }} ===Motor City Cruise (2022–2023)=== Nwaba was picked up off waivers by the [[Lakeland Magic]] of the G-League. But on December 17, 2022, Nwaba was traded to the [[Motor City Cruise]].{{cite web|title=2022-23 NBA G League Transactions|url=https://gleague.nba.com/transactions/|website=NBA.com|access-date=December 17, 2022}} In his debut for the Cruise during the regular season on December 27, 2022, Nwaba recorded 8 points, 9 rebounds, 3 assists and 2 steals in 34 minutes in a 108 - 115 loss to the [[Capital City Go-Go]].{{cite web | title=CCG vs MCC | url=https://stats.gleague.nba.com/game/2022200003/ }} For his first season with the Cruise, Nwaba played in 25 games and averaged 16.0 points, 8.8 rebounds and 3.2 assists in 32.7 minutes. On October 21, 2023, Nwaba signed with the [[Detroit Pistons]],{{cite tweet|author=Pistons PR|title=The @DetroitPistons announced today that the team has signed Treveon Graham, David Nwaba, Nate Roberts and Ryan Turell to {{as written|Ex|ibit [sic]}} 10 contracts.|number=1715746303668289656|user=Pistons_PR|date=October 21, 2023|access-date=October 30, 2023}} but was waived the same day.{{cite web|first=Luke|last=Adams|title=Pistons Sign, Waive David Nwaba, Three Others|url=https://www.hoopsrumors.com/2023/10/pistons-sign-waive-david-nwaba-three-others.html|website=HoopsRumors.com|date=October 21, 2023|access-date=October 30, 2023}} Nine days later, he re-joined the Motor City Cruise.{{cite tweet|author=Motor City Cruise|title=The engine is revving, and we're ready to roll! Check out the Motor City Cruise training camp roster - we're ready to work! #HustleAndDrive|number=1719088094782132699|user=MotorCityCruise|date=October 30, 2023|access-date=November 8, 2023}} For his second season with the Cruise, Nwaba would only play in 3 games during the regular season averaging 14.0 points and 5.3 rebounds. After his final game with the Cruise on December 30, 2023, he would leave the team in order to play professionally overseas. ===London Lions (2024)=== On January 8, 2024, Nwaba signed with the [[London Lions (basketball)|London Lions]] of the [[British Basketball League]].{{cite web|title=LONDON LIONS SIGN DAVID NWABA|url=https://www.thelondonlions.com/news/london-lions-sign-david-nwaba|website=TheLondonLions.com|date=January 8, 2024|access-date=January 9, 2024}} ===San-en NeoPhoenix (2024–present)=== On July 24, 2024, Nwaba signed with the [[San-en NeoPhoenix]] of the [[B.League]].{{cite web |title=デイビッド・ヌワバ選手 契約締結（新規）のお知らせ |url=https://www.neophoenix.jp/news/detail/id=20739 |publisher=三遠ネオフェニックス |access-date=October 1, 2024 |date=July 24, 2024}} ==NBA career statistics== {{NBA player statistics legend}} ===Regular season=== {{NBA player statistics start}} |- | style="text-align:left;"|{{nbay|2016}} | style="text-align:left;"|[[2016–17 Los Angeles Lakers season|L.A.
